text.p: Shares in utilities group Lyonnaise des Eaux and holding company Cie de Suez dropped sharply on Wednesday amid uncertainty over the terms of their planned merger, traders said.
Lyonnaise shed 3.43 percent to 535 francs, while Suez eased 1.99 percent to 278.2 while the market was down 1.51 percent.

An equity saleswoman said yield funds which had bought Suez on hopes of getting a big special payment were both unclear on the basis of the payout calculation and disappointed that there would apparently be only one overall dividend capped at some 20 francs per share, which includes the special payment.

Fund managers had estimated the 22-25 francs per share payout on the basis of 10 percent of Suez's estimated 34 billion francs in financial assets, as suggested on Wednesday by the chairman of Saint-Gobain, one of Suez shareholders.
A Suez spokeswoman said the company would be paying one single dividend but could not comment on the 20 franc total.

Investors were also unsure whether the capital gain would be calculated at the parent company or group level and whether the 500 million franc provision for the sale of Axashares would be reflected in the payout.
The spokeswoman said the capital gain would be based on the parent company accounts.
Lyonnaise's fall was attributed to the bursting of the speculative bubble which has surrounded the stock since the merger attracted the market's attention, the saleswoman said.
The merger is "fully priced in" and investors had little to look forward to as any operational benefits from the merger would take time to come through.
Analysts expect Lyonnaise to post 1996 net attributable profit of between one and 1.5 billion francs when it reports on Thursday.
